title: Cycle Detection in Directed Graph (BFS)
problemStatement: Given a directed graph with n nodes, detect whether it contains a cycle. Use Kahn’s BFS (indegree peeling): if you cannot order all n nodes, a cycle exists.
example:
n = 4
edges: 0→1, 1→2, 2→3, 3→1

Kahn takes 0, then stalls — nodes 1,2,3 remain with indegree > 0 → cycle = true

Without 3→1 the graph is a DAG → cycle = false, topo = [0,1,2,3]
intuition: In a DAG, Kahn eventually peels every node. A directed cycle traps a set of nodes that never reach indegree 0. So “processed count < n” is exactly cycle detection — same code as topo sort, different return value.

approaches.title: DFS 3-color (also correct)
approaches.idea: Back-edge to a node still on the recursion stack ⇒ directed cycle.
limitations: This topic focuses on the BFS/Kahn view

approaches.title: Optimal for this topic: Kahn BFS
approaches.idea: Run topo Kahn. If order length < n → cycle.
algorithm: Peel; count how many nodes were taken
approaches.code:
from collections import defaultdict, deque

def has_cycle_kahn(n, edges):
    g = defaultdict(list)
    indeg = [0] * n
    for u, v in edges:
        g[u].append(v)
        indeg[v] += 1
    q = deque([i for i in range(n) if indeg[i] == 0])
    taken = 0
    while q:
        u = q.popleft()
        taken += 1
        for v in g[u]:
            indeg[v] -= 1
            if indeg[v] == 0:
                q.append(v)
    return taken != n  # True ⇒ cycle
approaches.dryRun:
Start: indeg=[0,2,1,1], queue=[0]
Take 0 → indeg[1]=1, queue empty
taken=1 < 4 → cycle
approaches.whyWorks: Nodes on a directed cycle keep positive indegree forever inside the peel.

specialTechnique.title: BFS cycle check = failed topo
specialTechnique.body:
Topo Sort and Directed Cycle (BFS) are the same algorithm.
- Need an order → return the list (or [] on cycle)
- Need a boolean → return taken != n

DFS cycle check uses the recursion-stack color instead.

edgeCases: Cycle not reachable from an indegree-0 source (still detected — leftover nodes)
commonMistakes: Using undirected-cycle parent logic on a digraph
Stopping after finding one indegree-0 component and ignoring leftovers
Confusing this topic with plain BFS shortest path
